item.title: #2980380: Inline error messages are not using proper theming mechanisms
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +85/−18 · php +57/−18 · twig +28
  • Diff: bdba9f8
  • Discussion: #2980380 · 9 contributors · 39 comments
  • Followers: 17
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 9 contributors

Summary

The error summary that Inline Form Errors shows at the top of a form, such as "3 errors have been found:" followed by links to the fields, now renders through a real Twig template. Before, the module built it as a raw render array, so themes had nothing to override. Themes and sites can now customize its markup, for example to match a base theme's alert styling, and can target a single form. The default output is almost the same as before. The only visible change is a <span> around the count text.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The "N errors have been found:" summary now renders through a template, and the count text is wrapped in a new <span>.
  • New API: New inline_form_errors_summary theme hook with inline_form_errors_summary.html.twig and an inline_form_errors_summary__FORM_ID suggestion.

Technical details

FormErrorHandler::displayErrorMessages() used to build the summary from a #markup plural string plus an item_list render array. It now builds one render array with #theme => 'inline_form_errors_summary', #error_links and #form_id (taken from $form['#form_id']), then passes it to renderInIsolation() and addError(). Each link is wrapped as ['value' => <link renderable>] so the list is fed to item-list.html.twig as items.

InlineFormErrorsThemeHooks gains a hook_theme() implementation declaring the error_links and form_id variables. It also gains a hook_theme_suggestions_inline_form_errors_summary() implementation that adds inline_form_errors_summary__FORM_ID when a form ID is present. The new inline_form_errors_summary.html.twig uses {% trans %} with plural handling for the count, wraps the count text in a <span>, and includes item-list.html.twig with context: {list_style: 'comma-list'}.

FormErrorHandlerTest was refactored because the render array shape changed, and a test was added that checks the #theme, #form_id and #error_links values. PathAliasTest assertions were split into two statusMessageContains() calls because the span changes the whitespace around the text. Field-level inline error markup and the fieldset case from the original report were not touched. Only the summary got a template.

Upgrade

To customize the summary, copy core/modules/inline_form_errors/templates/inline_form_errors_summary.html.twig into your theme. To target one form, name the copy after its form ID, for example inline_form_errors_summary--node-article-form.html.twig. Hyphens replace underscores in template filenames. Code that parsed the old summary text directly (for example 1 error has been found: URL alias) should allow for the new <span> around the count text.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 19, 2018
  • Committed: October 28, 2026 (8 years later)

Key contributors

  • jrockowitz (The Big Blue House)
  • markhalliwell (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • pameeela
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • dcam

Collaboration

The issue was opened in 2018 around a Bootstrap theming need and sat idle for years. smustgrave picked it up from #2880011 and opened the MR. dcam reviewed it and suggested approaches. nicxvan pointed to item-list as the right template for a list. The final version moved the markup into a template that includes item-list.html.twig. alexpott committed it to main and also backported it to 12.0.x as a non-disruptive minor bug fix, since the markup change is only a new span and a change record covers the new template.

item.title:
#2350049: filter_autop() returns
but should return
for HTML5
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +8/−8 · php +8/−8
  • Diff: aad4f74
  • Discussion: #2350049 · 21 contributors · 75 comments
  • Followers: 29
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 21 contributors

Summary

The "Convert line breaks into HTML (i.e. <br> and <p>)" text filter now emits HTML5 style <br> for single line breaks instead of the XHTML style <br />. Browsers render both the same, but any custom test, snapshot or string match that expects the literal <br /> from this filter will need updating. It was committed to main and backported to 12.0.x, because Drupal 12 should be fully HTML5 and the maintainer judged it low risk.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Text run through the "Convert line breaks into HTML" filter (FilterAutoP) now contains <br> instead of <br /> in rendered output.

Technical details

The line-break logic lives in FilterAutoP::process() (the former _filter_autop()). The "make line breaks" regexes now insert and look for <br>: (?<!<br>)\s*\n is replaced with <br>\n, and the two cleanup regexes around block-level tags and p|li|div|dl|dd|dt|th|pre|td|ul|ol match <br>. The earlier step that collapses two consecutive breaks into a paragraph break was widened to <br ?/?>\s*<br ?/?>, so input that already contains <br>, <br/> or <br /> is still collapsed. Only the output side is switched to <br>.

The merged change touches FilterAutoP and FilterKernelTest only. The test expectations in testLineBreakFilter() were updated to <br>. In testHtmlCorrectorFilter() only the assertion message changed: Html::normalize('<br></br>') still yields <br><br>, which is why the description now says it is transformed into two br tags. Earlier review (catch, wim leers) noted that Html::normalize() and the filter system already emit HTML5 serialization since #2441811, which is why this filter was one of the remaining places still producing <br />. The parent effort is #1388926. A reviewer (nod_) asked whether the old <br /> forms could still occur, for example from CKEditor 4 configuration, which is why the first regex still accepts all three spellings.

item.title: #2735997: Decimal separator and precision settings unavailable when aggregating decimal fields
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +216/−7 · php +169/−7 · yml +47
  • Diff: cf863a1
  • Discussion: #2735997 · 30 contributors · 122 comments
  • Followers: 45

Summary

When a View uses aggregation (Sum, Average and similar) on a Decimal or Float field, the field settings now include the Round, Precision and Decimal point options. Before, those options were missing for aggregated decimal fields, so you could not control decimal places or the decimal separator in the output. Base decimal fields on entity types also now get numeric filter and contextual filter (argument) handlers instead of the generic standard ones. An earlier attempt at this issue was reverted after it broke COUNT and date aggregation output. This version leaves the aggregation handler override alone.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: Views field definitions for decimal and float fields now carry 'float' => TRUE, which exposes precision and decimal point settings on aggregated fields.

Technical details

When aggregation is on, Sql::getAggregationInfo() swaps in the numeric field handler for functions like Sum and Average. NumericField::buildOptionsForm() only shows precision and decimal point settings when the handler definition contains float => TRUE, and Views data never set that flag for decimal or float fields. The fix sets $data[...]['field']['float'] = TRUE in two places. FieldViewsDataProvider::defaultFieldImplementation() does it for configurable fields whose schema column type is float or numeric, which covers the decimal field type. EntityViewsData::mapSingleFieldViewsData() does it for base fields.

In EntityViewsData, the numeric column type was previously unhandled and fell into the default branch. It is now grouped with float, double and decimal, so base decimal fields get the numeric argument and filter plugins. The common field and sort ids were hoisted above the column-type switch. Integer columns keep the numeric argument and filter but get no float flag.

This is the second attempt. The first commit removed the field => numeric override from getAggregationInfo(), which caused regressions (see #3517853, #3518896) and was reverted. The form submit exception found along the way was split to #3613882. Tests added: kernel tests for FieldViewsDataProvider and EntityViewsData, a QueryGroupByTest::testAggregateDecimalOutput() check that a summed value of 5.789 renders as 5,79, and a FieldUITest functional test. The commit landed on main and 12.0.x, and was backported to 11.x and 11.5.x.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 29, 2016
  • Committed: October 22, 2026 (10 years later)

Key contributors

  • mschudders
  • nikita_tt
  • lendude (iO)
  • playful
  • ranjith_kumar_k_u (Zyxware Technologies)
  • joelpittet (The University of British Columbia)
  • asad_ahmed (OpenSense Labs)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • ben greenberg
  • ramil g (The University of British Columbia)

Collaboration

The first fix removed the numeric handler override from getAggregationInfo(). It was committed, then reverted after regressions were reported. acbramley reported the COUNT and date output regressions, argued that the override is required for aggregated output, and prepared the revert MR. joelpittet then reworked the MR to keep the override and set the float flag in the Views data instead. acbramley retested the change on the affected client site and asked for test coverage of the decimal output, which the MR then gained.

item.title: #3082239: Forbid limited length primary and unique keys, allow only in indexes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +363/−33 · php +363/−33
  • Diff: 2be6e06
  • Discussion: #3082239 · 9 contributors · 59 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Partial (prefix) column lengths are now documented as valid only for indexes, not for primary or unique keys. Code that passes a column with a length, such as ['name', 10], in a primary key or unique key now triggers a deprecation notice. In Drupal 13 it will throw a SchemaException. Core has no such keys, so this mainly affects contrib and custom modules. Those should specify full columns, or move the partial-length columns to an index.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Specifying a column length (e.g. [['name', 10]]) in a primary key or unique key is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will throw a SchemaException in drupal:13.0.0. Schema::ensureNotNullPrimaryKey() is deprecated in favour of validatePrimaryKeySchema().
  • New API: New protected Schema::validatePrimaryKeySchema() and Schema::validateUniqueKeySchema() methods for driver implementations.

Technical details

The check runs in the shared Schema base class and is called from the MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite drivers. It covers createTable(), addPrimaryKey(), addUniqueKey(), addField() and changeField(). validatePrimaryKeySchema() emits the deprecation when any primary key column is an array. It also keeps the existing check that primary key fields are not null, which replaces ensureNotNullPrimaryKey(). validateUniqueKeySchema() emits the deprecation for unique keys. In the 12.x deprecation period the request is still processed. The PostgreSQL driver already ignored prefix lengths for primary and unique keys, and the deprecation message describes the length as disregarded.

The addField() primary key detection in the MySQL and PostgreSQL drivers now uses fieldNames(), so array-form key columns are handled. The PrimaryKey and UniqueKey value object docblocks no longer mention length arrays, and the Database API docs now say that partial length is for indexes only. The existing SchemaUniquePrefixedKeysIndexTestBase driver tests now expect the deprecation. A @todo notes that they should test full-length columns once 13.0.0 lands (#3615136). The change record is https://www.drupal.org/node/3375071.

Upgrade

Replace partial-length columns in primary and unique keys with full columns, or move them to an index:

// Deprecated in 12.1.0, throws SchemaException in 13.0.0.
'primary key' => [['test_field_1', 10]],
'unique keys' => ['test_unique_key' => [['test_field_1', 10]]],

// Use full columns for the key...
'primary key' => ['test_field_1'],
// ...or put the partial length on an index.
'indexes' => ['test_index' => [['test_field_1', 10]]],

Custom driver code that calls ensureNotNullPrimaryKey() should call validatePrimaryKeySchema() instead.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 19, 2019
  • Committed: October 27, 2026 (7 years later)

  • daffie

item.title: #3594338: Add a command to import configuration
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +595/−43 · php +595/−43
  • Diff: 0a04f46
  • Discussion: #3594338 · 4 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's command line tool gains a config:import command (alias cim), the counterpart to config:export (#3594337). It imports the staged configuration from the sync storage into the active site, the same way the Configuration module's synchronize page does, but from the terminal. It prints a table of the pending creates, updates, deletes and renames, asks for confirmation (skippable with --yes / -y), then runs the import and reports success or errors. It is part of the CLI in Core initiative (#3582246).

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ConfigImportCommand is marked @internal and uses Symfony Console attributes (#[AsCommand], #[Option]). It runs the sync storage through ImportStorageTransformer, so import transform event subscribers apply. It builds a StorageComparer against the active storage and exits successfully with "There are no changes to import." when nothing differs. Otherwise it renders the change list and asks for confirmation. Declining throws UserAbortException. The command then gets a ConfigImporter from ConfigImporterFactory. If alreadyImporting() is true, it warns that another request may be synchronizing and returns failure. Otherwise it calls validate() and import(). A ConfigImporterException (for example the site UUID mismatch) is printed as an error and returns failure. Errors collected on the importer also produce failure, with each error printed.

The renderTable() method that previously lived in ConfigExportCommand moved into a new ConfigCommandTrait, now used by both commands, so the export and import commands share the same change table. The functional test in the diff notes that batch errors are not shown, because the command line does not run batches yet.

Contribution

  • Opened: June 9, 2026
  • Committed: October 26, 2026 (4 months later)

item.title: #3623862: Rename hook_system_info_alter to hook_extension_info_alter
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 51 files, +183/−153 · php +179/−149 · yml +4/−4
  • Diff: 8797dc9
  • Discussion: #3623862 · 5 contributors · 20 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

The hook for altering the data parsed from module and theme .info.yml files is now called hook_extension_info_alter(). The old name, hook_system_info_alter(), suggested the System module provides it, which is not the case. The old hook still works but is deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Alter hook for extension info renamed from system_info to extension_info; the old hook is still invoked but triggers a deprecation.
  • Deprecation: hook_system_info_alter() is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and removed from drupal:13.0.0, in favor of hook_extension_info_alter().
  • New API: New hook_extension_info_alter(array &$info, Extension $file, $type) for altering module and theme .info.yml data.

Technical details

ExtensionList::doList() now calls $this->moduleHandler->alter('extension_info', ...) for each extension. It then calls alterDeprecated() with the system_info hook name and a message pointing to the change record https://www.drupal.org/node/3624723. Existing hook_system_info_alter() implementations therefore keep running and emit a deprecation. Both hooks are invoked, the new one first. The thread discussed ordering and concluded it should not matter much, since an implementor who cares can guard with a class property or check the altered values.

In core.api.php, hook_extension_info_alter() is documented and hook_system_info_alter() is marked @deprecated. Core's own test module implementations were renamed to #[Hook('extension_info_alter')]. Test state keys and the update_test.settings config key system_info also became extension_info, but these are test-only. The ModuleExtensionList comment and a ProjectInfo comment were updated to the new name.

The issue targeted the new hook at 12.1.0, with removal of the old one in 13.0.0. It was not added to 11.x. The change record explains how to support both versions in the meantime.

Upgrade

Rename your implementation. In an OOP hook class:

#[Hook('extension_info_alter')]
public function extensionInfoAlter(array &$info, Extension $file, $type): void {
  // ...
}

Replace #[Hook('system_info_alter')] and hook_system_info_alter() implementations before Drupal 13. See the change record https://www.drupal.org/node/3624723 for keeping 11.x support.

  • Committed: October 26, 2026 (1 month later)

item.title: #3575547: Deprecate StatementPrefetchIterator
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +121/−58 · php +121/−58
  • Diff: 8582e13
  • Discussion: #3575547 · 3 contributors · 12 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

StatementPrefetchIterator is deprecated. Only the SQLite driver extended it, and StatementBase is now the base class for statements, so the middle class no longer serves a purpose. The SQLite Statement now extends StatementBase directly. Contrib or custom database drivers that extend StatementPrefetchIterator get a deprecation notice and should move to StatementBase. Per the committer, this may be the first 12.1-only deprecation to land.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: \Drupal\Core\Database\StatementPrefetchIterator is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0; extend \Drupal\Core\Database\Statement\StatementBase instead.

Technical details

StatementPrefetchIterator now triggers E_USER_DEPRECATED when the file is loaded and in its constructor. It is marked deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will be removed in drupal:13.0.0. The change record is https://www.drupal.org/node/3575664.

The SQLite Statement class now extends StatementBase, uses PdoTrait, and has its own constructor. It takes over the prefetch logic in a new protected executeAndPrefetch(). That method dispatches the statement execution start, failure and end events, then runs the statement. It reads all rows into a PrefetchedResult and releases the client statement so no SELECT lock stays open. execute() still retries once on SQLite error 17 (schema change), and it now applies the fetch option itself with setFetchMode() after execution.

getClientStatement(): \PDOStatement previously existed as a duplicate in StatementPrefetchIterator and StatementWrapperIterator. It is now implemented once in PdoTrait, which replaces the abstract declaration there. The thrown exception type documented in its docblock changes from \RuntimeException to \LogicException, matching what the code actually throws. The unit test that instantiated StatementPrefetchIterator now uses an anonymous StatementBase subclass.

Upgrade

Drivers extending the deprecated class should extend StatementBase and implement the prefetch logic themselves. The SQLite driver now does this:

use Drupal\Core\Database\Statement\PdoTrait;
use Drupal\Core\Database\Statement\StatementBase;

class Statement extends StatementBase {
  use PdoTrait;
}

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 24, 2026
  • Committed: October 26, 2026 (8 months later)

item.title: #3218381: #file_value_callbacks bypass the TrustedCallbackInterface protections
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +72/−7 · php +72/−7
  • Diff: ecc5d94
  • Discussion: #3218381 · 6 contributors · 24 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

The managed_file form element accepted #file_value_callbacks and called whatever was listed there, bypassing the trusted callback protections added in #2966327 to limit remote code execution through render arrays. Those callbacks are now checked the same way as other render callbacks. In Drupal 12.1 an untrusted callback still runs but triggers a deprecation. In Drupal 13.0 it will throw an exception. Custom and contrib code that uses #file_value_callbacks needs updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Closes a bypass of the trusted callback protections: arbitrary callables in #file_value_callbacks were executed unchecked.
  • Deprecation: Using #file_value_callbacks callbacks on managed_file that are not #[TrustedCallback]-tagged methods, TrustedCallbackInterface methods or anonymous functions is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will throw in drupal:13.0.0.

Technical details

ManagedFile::valueCallback() used to run $callback($element, $input, $form_state) for each entry in #file_value_callbacks. It now passes each one to StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback() with a custom message. That message says untrusted callbacks are deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will throw in drupal:13.0.0, and it links to https://www.drupal.org/node/3620771. StaticTrustedCallbackHelper no longer supports a silenced deprecation (#3081025). The code therefore catches UntrustedCallbackException, calls @trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_DEPRECATED), and then still invokes the callback, which keeps the deprecation period working. The %%s in the sprintf() format is intentional: it leaves a %s placeholder for the helper to fill in with the callback. Trusted callbacks are methods tagged #[TrustedCallback], methods of a TrustedCallbackInterface class, and anonymous functions. Kernel test coverage was added in the file module's managed file element test. A comment on the issue notes that contrib has copied this pattern into other elements, and follow-up issues are probably needed for them.

Upgrade

Tag any #file_value_callbacks callback method with the attribute used in the core test:

use Drupal\Core\Security\Attribute\TrustedCallback;

#[TrustedCallback]
public function managedFileValueCallbackTrusted(array &$element, $input, FormStateInterface $form_state): void {
  // ...
}

Alternatively, implement TrustedCallbackInterface on the class or use an anonymous function. Plain function names such as 'die' are no longer trusted. They trigger a deprecation in 12.1 and will throw in 13.0.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: June 11, 2021
  • Committed: October 23, 2026 (5 years later)

item.title: #3398033: Fix deprecated assert.active directive
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +11/−6 · php +6/−4 · htaccess +5/−2
  • Diff: e180d54
  • Discussion: #3398033 · 15 contributors · 66 comments
  • Followers: 32
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 15 contributors

Summary

The scaffolded .htaccess no longer sets the assert.active PHP directive, which is deprecated in PHP 8.3 and can log a deprecation under Apache with mod_php. It now sets zend.assertions to 0 (assertions compiled in but skipped). Comments recommend 1 on development machines and 0 or -1 in production. The fix was committed to main and backported to 12.0.x, 11.x, 11.5.x, 11.4.x, 11.3.x and 10.6.x. Release managers said it needs a release note because it changes a scaffolded, site-owner-managed file.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Scaffolded .htaccess now sets php_value zend.assertions 0 instead of php_value assert.active 0.

Technical details

The .htaccess template (php_value assert.active 0 inside <IfModule mod_php.c>) is replaced with php_value zend.assertions 0, plus a comment pointing to the PHP manual. The header comment is reworded to say the block is for PHP settings that cannot be changed at runtime. The docblock in default.settings.php is also updated. It now says to set zend.assertions=1 in php.ini on development machines and 0 or -1 in production, with a @see link to the PHP manual. It no longer claims the setting cannot be changed from .htaccess.

Background from the thread: #3375693 removed the assert_options() calls and the assertion-enabling code in example.settings.local.php. It left assert.active 0 in .htaccess. Under Apache with mod_php, that value still takes effect. A settings.local.php that only sets zend.assertions therefore could not turn assertions back on. Using zend.assertions in .htaccess restores the documented way to enable them.

The thread notes that zend.assertions can only be fully enabled or disabled in php.ini. If php.ini sets it to -1, the .htaccess line can trigger a PHP warning in the Apache log. Participants suggested that such sites remove the line or ignore the warning. A related question, whether tests should force assertions on, was split off to a gitlab_templates issue (3500234).

Upgrade

Existing sites keep their current .htaccess, because it is a scaffolded file. To pick up the change, update the block manually or re-scaffold:

<IfModule mod_php.c>
  php_value zend.assertions 0
</IfModule>

If your PHP config sets zend.assertions to -1, you can remove that line.

item.title: #3471113: Update to selenium/standalone-chrome:134+
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +17/−1 · php +14 · yml +3/−1
  • Diff: 9faf7e2
  • Discussion: #3471113 · 7 contributors · 60 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Core's FunctionalJavascript tests now run against a current Chrome in CI (pinned to 155.0 in the commit on main, previously 133.0) instead of an old one. Since Chrome 134, a WebDriver click could return before the page navigation had started, so tests randomly read the old page. Core's Selenium driver now turns off the Chrome feature behind this. Local, CI and contrib test runs that use Drupal's driver get the fix, with no test changes needed. This does not change site runtime behavior.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The cause is Chrome's DeferRendererTasksAfterInput feature, on by default since Chrome 134. It delays some page tasks until the next frame after an input event. .gitlab-ci.yml gets a new SELENIUM_CHROME_TAG variable, set to "155.0". The .with-selenium-chrome service now uses selenium/standalone-chrome:$SELENIUM_CHROME_TAG, and the job that runs with COMPOSER_UPDATE: "1" overrides the tag to latest. The issue text proposed 152.0, but the diff pins 155.0.

CKEditor5AllowedTagsTest::testFullHtml() is now skipped with markTestSkipped(). Newer ChromeDriver treats zero-height elements as not displayed, which exposed empty filter tips under text format selectors. That is tracked in #3621903.

The issue notes that Chromium has not formally shipped this feature, so a later Chrome may remove the flag. The alternative was waiting for two animation frames after each click and form submit. item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

  • Changes: 5 files, +78/−2 · php +72 · js +6/−2

Summary

Batch operations that run through the browser progress bar no longer break when a CDN or reverse proxy sorts query string parameters (Cloudflare "Query String Sort" and Fastly were reported). Before, the batch requests ended in a 406 "Not acceptable format: json" error and larger batches did not finish. The fix was backported to 11.4.x and later. Sites that worked around this with a page rule disabling query string sorting for /batch* can drop that rule after updating.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The initial batch URI already contains op=do_nojs. core/misc/batch.js appended a second op to it (&op=do for polling, &op=finished at the end). A proxy that sorts parameters alphabetically moved op=do_nojs last. PHP then used that value, so _batch_page() took the do_nojs branch for a _format=json request and returned an HTML render array, which triggered the 406.

The shipped fix is client side. batch.js now builds a URL from batch.uri and calls url.searchParams.set('op', ...) for both the do polling URL and the finished redirect, so each request carries exactly one op. An earlier approach (MR !15103, merged server side) treated do_nojs on non-HTML requests as do in _batch_page(). It was dropped because the duplicate parameter comes from Drupal's own JavaScript, so fixing it at the source was preferred. Both approaches got manual confirmation on Cloudflare.

The no-JS meta refresh path is unchanged. A FunctionalJavascript test (testBatchUrls) uses a new batch9 in the batch_test module. It checks that each polling request URL ends in /batch?_format=json&id=1&op=do and that the finished URL ends in /batch?id=1&op=finished.

item.title: #3513035: Add constraint to check that the max delta for a field item list does not exceed its cardinality
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +287/−0 · php +283 · yml +4
  • Diff: 20ac0fa
  • Discussion: #3513035 · 12 contributors · 77 comments
  • Followers: 15
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 12 contributors

Summary

Field storage config validation now rejects a cardinality lower than the number of values already stored for that field. Before, validation could not catch this. Setting cardinality to 1 on a field where some entity already holds 2 values now fails with a message like "The field 'field_int' of entity type 'entity_test' has more entries (2) than the cardinality (1) allows." Unlimited cardinality (-1) is always accepted. The change landed in main, and later comments record backports to 11.x and 11.5.x. It also unblocks the parent effort #3324140 to convert field storage and field config form validation into validation constraints.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: field.storage.*.* config schema: cardinality now carries the NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinality constraint.
  • New API: New NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinality validation constraint plugin (with entityType and fieldName options) in the field module.

Technical details

The constraint is a plugin class, Drupal\field\Plugin\Validation\Constraint\NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinality. It was originally named NoEntitiesExistYetWithHigherCardinality and was renamed because it counts field items, not entities. It takes entityType and fieldName options. field.storage.*.* in field.schema.yml wires it to the cardinality key using %parent.entity_type and %parent.field_name.

NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinalityValidator resolves those expressions with TypeResolver::resolveExpression() and skips validation in three cases:

  • The cardinality is unlimited.
  • The field_storage_config entity doesn't exist yet.
  • The storage has custom storage (hasCustomStorage()).

Otherwise it runs an aggregate entity query with MAX on field_name.%delta, with access checks off. It adds 1 to the result, because deltas start at 0, and adds a violation if that count is greater than the cardinality. An early version compared the raw max delta, which allowed two extra values. This was caught when a test was added that actually calls the validator.

The kernel test expects a SchemaIncompleteException when FieldStorageConfig::save() is called with the lowered cardinality. A unit test covers the constraint's defaults and message. The constructor uses explicit typed properties instead of the base Constraint option handling, because of the Symfony 7.4 deprecations (#3555534). Per the thread, the main commit has no exception handling in the validator, and the backport adds #[HasNamedArguments] and a catch for the exception that occurs in tests.

Summary

Core now has a generic delete form for bundle entities (content types, block types, media types, comment types and so on). If any content of that bundle exists, the form says so, hides the Delete button and keeps a Cancel button, which non-JS users need on the standalone page. Node, block content, media and comment types now use it. Their separate copies of this logic are gone, so the wording of the "you can't delete this" messages changes slightly. For example, nodes are now described as "content items" instead of "pieces of content". Contrib bundle entity types can use the same form instead of writing their own.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The delete forms for node, block content, media and comment types now render the blocking message and a Cancel button, built from the entity type labels. Markup and message wording differ from before.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Entity\Form\BundleEntityDeleteForm, a generic delete form for bundle entity types, with overridable getContentEntityCount() and getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion().

Technical details

Drupal\Core\Entity\Form\BundleEntityDeleteForm extends EntityDeleteForm. In buildForm() it reads getBundleOf() from the bundle entity type and throws a \LogicException if the type is not a bundle of anything. It then counts content entities of that bundle via getContentEntityCount(), using an entity query with accessCheck(FALSE) on the content entity type's bundle key. It also collects strings from getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion(), which returns an empty array by default. If either blocks deletion, the form shows each reason as a paragraph, changes the title to "Unable to delete @bundle-label %type", and returns only the actions element with submit removed. Otherwise it defers to the parent form. The messages use the singular and plural labels of both entity types, so a bundle entity type should define label_singular and label_plural for itself and for its content entity type to get good wording.

CommentTypeDeleteForm now extends this class. It overrides getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion() to report comment fields that still use the comment type. The @internal classes NodeTypeDeleteConfirm, BlockContentTypeDeleteForm and MediaTypeDeleteConfirmForm were deleted. The delete form handler on NodeType, BlockContentType and MediaType now points to BundleEntityDeleteForm. Tests in entity_test gain labels and edit-form and delete-form links for entity_test_bundle, plus a kernel test BundleDeleteFormTest. A follow-up commit fixed that test's namespace from Drupal\FunctionalTests\Entity to Drupal\KernelTests\Core\Entity.

The issue discussed a "delete all content" option, as Paragraphs offers. It was left out of scope. Core's DeleteMultipleForm does not yet support bundles, so this would need a follow-up.

Upgrade

Contrib bundle entity types that hand-roll a "can't delete while content exists" form can switch to the generic one in their entity type attribute:

use Drupal\Core\Entity\Form\BundleEntityDeleteForm;

handlers: [
  'form' => [
    'delete' => BundleEntityDeleteForm::class,
  ],
],

To add extra blocking conditions, extend it and override the method, as CommentTypeDeleteForm does:

protected function getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion(): array {
  $reasons = parent::getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion();
  $reasons[] = $this->t('...');
  return $reasons;
}

item.title: #3594335: Add a module and theme uninstall command
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +580/−38 · php +579/−38 · txt +1
  • Diff: 3b94128
  • Discussion: #3594335 · 9 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 14
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Drupal core now has an ex:uninstall console command (aliases exun, pm:uninstall, pmu) that uninstalls modules or themes from the command line. It takes a comma-separated list of machine names. It lists the extensions it will remove, including dependents pulled in automatically, and asks for confirmation before removing the dependents. --yes skips the prompt and --dry-run shows what would happen without changing anything. It is the counterpart to the ex:install command, as part of the CLI in Core initiative.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Both installer interfaces gained a new abstract method, so custom implementations of ModuleInstallerInterface or ThemeInstallerInterface must implement it.
  • New API: ModuleInstallerInterface::getModulesToUninstall() and ThemeInstallerInterface::getThemesToUninstall() resolve the full, ordered set of extensions an uninstall would remove.

Technical details

The command is Drupal\Core\Extension\Command\ExtensionUninstallCommand, marked @internal. It classifies each name as a module or theme, reports unknown names, and refuses to mix modules and themes in one invocation. It resolves the full set through the new getModulesToUninstall() or getThemesToUninstall() method. For modules it then runs validateUninstall(), the same checks as the uninstall form, and reports blockers before changing anything. In non-interactive mode, extra dependents without --yes throw UserAbortException.

To make this possible, the dependency resolution that used to sit inside ModuleInstaller::uninstall() and ThemeInstaller::uninstall() was extracted into the two new public interface methods. getModulesToUninstall() returns the installed modules to remove, including installed dependents when $uninstall_dependents is TRUE. They are sorted by module weight, the order uninstall() uses. It throws UnknownExtensionException for unknown modules or dependents. ModuleInstaller::uninstall() still returns FALSE in those cases, so its behavior for callers is unchanged.

getThemesToUninstall() throws for themes that are not installed, the default theme and the admin theme. With $uninstall_dependents TRUE it adds installed sub-themes to the list. ThemeInstaller::uninstall() passes FALSE, so it still throws if a base theme's sub-theme is not listed explicitly. ModulesUninstallConfirmForm::buildForm() now also calls getModulesToUninstall(), so the confirmation list includes dependents in uninstall order.

Upgrade

Custom classes implementing ModuleInstallerInterface or ThemeInstallerInterface must add the new methods:

public function getModulesToUninstall(array $module_list, bool $uninstall_dependents = TRUE): array;
public function getThemesToUninstall(array $theme_list, bool $uninstall_dependents = TRUE): array;

Kernel test classes that share their environment (via the ShareEnvironment attribute from #1411074) now build the container once for the first test method and load it from cache for the remaining methods. Test classes that don't share the environment behave as before for container building. In the author's measurements, a 26-method test went from about 19s to about 15s. With xhprof enabled, per-method time dropped from about 2.5s to about 700ms. The saving is smaller for tests that install modules in several methods.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: KernelTestBase::$container is now typed ?ContainerInterface instead of ?ContainerBuilder; KernelTestBase::$keyValue is now the booted container's keyvalue service rather than a memory factory.
  • New API: New @internal Drupal\Core\Test\KernelTestDrupalKernel and a protected DrupalKernel::getContainerFromCacheIfCacheable() hook.

Technical details

KernelTestBase::bootKernel() now creates a Drupal\Core\Test\KernelTestDrupalKernel (marked @internal) instead of a plain DrupalKernel, passing static::sharesEnvironment() as the cache flag. When the environment is shared, it calls setContainerNeedsRebuild(FALSE) and setOverrideUseCache(TRUE), so the first method compiles and caches the container and later methods load it. To support this, DrupalKernel::initializeContainer() now calls a new protected getContainerFromCacheIfCacheable(), which holds the old "module list not set and no forced rebuild" check, and the subclass overrides it. The subclass appends a cacheSuffix to getContainerCacheKey() and increments it in rebuildContainer() and resetContainer(). A container rebuilt inside a test method is therefore cached under its own key and does not overwrite the initial one. bootKernel() calls resetCacheSuffix() and then resetContainer(), so every method starts from the same cached initial container with fresh service state. There is an @todo pointing at #2218651.

KernelTestBase no longer registers its own synthetic keyvalue service (memory factory, or database factory for shared environments). The container's normal key value service is used, and $this->keyValue is set from $this->container->get('keyvalue') after boot. As a result the key_value table now exists in kernel test databases. Core tests were adjusted: SchemaTest expected table lists now include key_value, a menu link content test lists key_value among its tables, and the installer test drops key_value in setUp() so the installer sees an uninstalled site. $container is now typed ?ContainerInterface. A new KernelTestSharedContainerTest uses the container_rebuild_test module's counter to assert the container is built once across three data-provider iterations. Follow-ups were opened for sharing caches between methods (#3629052) and deprecating KernelTestBase::$keyValue (#3629287). The PhpDumper container work in #3583505 is expected to be compatible with this approach.

Upgrade

Core tests that inspect the database table list needed key_value added, for example in SchemaTest:

$this->assertEquals(['config', 'key_value', 'select'], $tables);

Contrib kernel tests that type-hint $this->container as ContainerBuilder or assume an in-memory $this->keyValue may need adjusting. In the issue thread the committer expected existing tests to keep working and planned to update the shared-environment change record (https://www.drupal.org/node/3623403) with conversion steps.
